INTELLIGENT WILDLIFE AND WANDERING CATTLE DETECTION AND TRACKING SYSTEM WITH UNSUPERVISED LEARNING APPROACH USING DBSCAN

The growing incidence of human-wildlife conflict and the proliferation of stray cattle pose significant challenges to agricultural productivity, road safety, and ecological balance. Conventional detection and tracking methods, including manual observation, camera traps, and RFID tagging, have limitations in real-time monitoring, scalability, and adaptability across diverse habitats. Although supervised deep learning achieves strong animal classification performance, it requires large labeled datasets and may struggle with unfamiliar environments or species.

This work proposes an intelligent wildlife and stray cattle monitoring framework based on unsupervised learning, using Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) to detect and track animals without labeled training data. The system processes multimodal sensor inputs, including visible-light camera streams, thermal infrared imagery, and motion sensor readings, through a sequential pipeline. First, optical flow and background subtraction are used for feature extraction. Next, DBSCAN performs spatial clustering to identify individual animals or groups. Finally, optimal transport-based temporal association tracks detected clusters across successive frames.

The framework was evaluated using publicly available camera trap datasets. Results achieved an F1-score of 0.87 for animal detection and a 92.3% noise rejection rate, while maintaining reliable tracking under challenging environmental conditions. By eliminating dependence on labeled datasets, the proposed approach can be rapidly deployed across different regions, weather conditions, and habitats. Overall, the framework provides a cost-effective and scalable solution supporting wildlife conservation, agricultural protection, ecological monitoring, and the reduction of human-animal conflicts.

PSO Based Ensemble Method for Intrusion Detection in Heterogeneous Networks

Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) that use one Machine Learning (ML) model suffer from being inefficient in detecting novel attacks, having low detection rates and high false-positive rates and failing to generalize well on heterogeneous environments. In this paper, a hybrid ensemble-based IDS solution, that consists of three base learners with distinct inductive biases, including Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and fuzzy membership based classification, is proposed. Instead of averaging their outcomes, PSO algorithm, which is a gradient-free search technique, is used for finding optimal soft-voting weights for maximizing the validation F1 score. To solve class imbalance, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is used for the training set only, thus avoiding information leakage to the validation and test sets. The proposed IDS framework was tested on three benchmark IDS datasets, including NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15 and WSN-DS. The latter one contains wireless sensor network data. The proposed ensemble, with PSO-optimized weights, outperforms all base classifiers on accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score and provides 98.95\%, 98.98% and 99.65\% accuracy scores, respectively, and increases the F1 score of the rare U2R class of NSL-KDD to 83.21%.Ablation study analyses the impact of fuzzy contribution and PSO compared to an equal weight allocation, grid search, and random search, while cost analysis is done for training and testing times. Comparison with previous literature puts the work in the context of related studies using PSO and heterogeneous ensemble IDSs. The findings show that learning dataset-dependent fusion weights is an effective solution for achieving reliable detection in heterogeneous networks including IoT-based ones.

Quantum Feature Map-Enhanced Classical Random Forest for   Diabetes  Prediction Using the Dia-Health Bangladeshi Dataset

Diabetes mellitus is a major chronic health condition that requires early detection and accurate prediction to support timely medical intervention. This study proposes a quantum feature map-enhanced classical machine learning framework for diabetes prediction using the DiaHealth Bangladeshi Dataset, containing 5,437 records and 14 independent attributes. The proposed approach combines quantum feature mapping with classical ensemble learning to explore the effectiveness of quantum-based feature representations in healthcare classification. Initially, categorical data are transformed using Label Encoding, and numerical features are standardized using StandardScaler. Six input features are then mapped into quantum state representations using Qiskit's ZZFeatureMap with two repetitions. The real-valued components of the resulting statevector are extracted to generate 64-dimensional feature representations. These features are passed to a classical Random Forest classifier consisting of 100 decision trees, which uses majority voting to classify individuals as diabetic or non-diabetic. The preliminary experimental results report an accuracy of 93.68%, weighted precision of 87.75%, weighted recall of 93.68%, and weighted F1-score of 90.62%. However, further validation is required because preprocessing before data partitioning may introduce data leakage. This study demonstrates a hybrid quantum-classical approach for diabetes prediction and highlights the potential of quantum feature mapping in machine learning-based healthcare applications. Future work will focus on leakage-free preprocessing, systematic feature selection, comparison with classical models, and evaluation using real quantum hardware.

An IoT-Driven Geo-Tracking and Predictive Alert System for Smart Waste Collection Optimization

Abstract
With rapid urbanisation, the amount of waste produced in urban areas is growing and commences to put pressure on the waste collection system that is organised based on a programmed waste collection and manual recording. These limitations result in lower-than-average resource usage, higher costs and/or environmental issues. In this paper, GeoSmartWasteAI, a smart grid-based frame work for Geo tracking and prediction-based alert system for optimisation of waste collection process adopting IoT approach is presented. The designed system include implementation of a lightweight Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for the Prediction of Waste Management Efficiency, geospatial intelligence and waste management data analytics to identify the critical situations WHERE waste is farmed. To enhance the robustness of the model and its learning capacity, techniques such as data cleaning, encoding and normalisation are used. Geo-tracking can also be used to monitor locations and if overflow is occurring a predictive alert system can be used to take proactive action. The experimental assessment carried out using classification criteria and visualisation-based analysis shows good prediction and decision support. The system proposed is a scalable smart waste management system for the smart city emphasizing on the collection of waste, utilization of waste as resources and protection of environment.

Slotify: A Smart Web-Based Online Appointment Scheduling Platform for Service-Based Businesses

Small and medium service-oriented enterprises
clinics, grooming studios, coaching centres, and consultancy firms– still coordinate bookings largely by phone and paper register, a habit that routinely produces double-booked slots, forgotten appointments, and staff time that nobody bothers to account for. This paper presents Slotify, a browser-accessible, multitenant booking platform built on the MERN stack (MongoDB,Express.js, React.js, Node.js) that lets independent businesses onboard under their own public storefront while sharing a single application instance. The system’s central engineering contribution is a slot-availability engine that resolves staff working hours, breaks, holidays, buffer times, and advance-booking windows into a live grid of open slots, backed by a database enforced unique constraint that makes a race-condition double
booking structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely
in practice. We document the architecture, the booking and
reschedule algorithms in pseudocode, and a feature-by-feature
comparison against three commercial platforms actually in use
today– Calendly, Booksy, and Fresha– as well as two previously published academic prototypes. Unlike prior systems, which each cover a fragment of the scheduling lifecycle, Slotify combines tenant-scoped multi-staff scheduling, audited reschedule history, and a public discovery layer without per-seat licensing or marketplace commission. We close by discussing, with reference to existing clinical and operational literature rather than unverified benchmarks of our own, where the architecture is expected to help and where its current single-location, English-only scope still falls short of production-grade commercial offerings.

The increasing use of IoT devices in cyber-physical systems has made network security a major issue. This paper presents IoT-SrcAI, a hybrid framework for network traffic analysis which utilizes two complementary paths: an anomaly detection path and an attack classification path. The architecture (as shown in Fig. 1) consists of data pre-processing, feature representation, an Autoencoder based anomaly detector, a CNN–Bi-LSTM–Attention based classifier, explainability, decision fusion and an alert and feedback stage. The experiments described in the paper use the NSL-KDD benchmark and the DoS, Probe, R2L and U2R attack categories. The baseline models reported are logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest and an Autoencoder based detector. The results table in the paper report 97.80% accuracy for Logistic Regression, 88.60% for Random Forest and 99.89% for Iot-SrcAI. These results need to be cross checked against the original test outputs before any firm conclusions can be drawn, in particular to ensure that the baseline and proposed framework results are using the same data split and evaluation procedure. The paper is focused on the framework and its benchmark evaluation; any claims about live deployment, zero-day detection or real time operation are only made where such claims are directly supported by the experimental results.

Blockchain-Integrated Genetic Algorithm for Cost-Optimal Agri-Supply Chain Distribution: A Single-Objective Instantiation of the BLOCK-MOO-ASC Framework

Fresh produce loses value in transit, yet agricultural allocation models rarely use observed transit times. This paper studies the cost objective of BLOCK-MOO-ASC, a proposed multi-objective framework in which a permissioned ledger would supply shipment telemetry to optimisation models. We model farm-to-distribution-centre shipment allocation with a per-ton spoilage cost derived from each leg's transit time through first-order freshness decay. With fixed transit times this model is a linear transportation problem, which linear programming solves exactly. Adding whole-truck dispatch costs introduces a genuine decision-dependent nonlinearity and yields a fixed-charge, mixed-integer model. We solve it exactly with a mixed-integer solver and approxi-mately with a random-key genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimisa-tion, differential evolution and simulated annealing under one encoding, ob-jective and evaluation budget, and with four constructive heuristics, on eighteen seeded instances (5–40 farms, 4–30 centres) with up to 30 runs per method; all data and code are published. The exact solver proved optimality on every instance up to 10×8 and, even when limited to the GA's run time, outperformed all metaheuristics. The GA's mean gap to the best known solu-tion was 1.35–2.38%, slightly behind differential evolution, while greedy and Vogel heuristics were 4.0–14.6% worse. A value-of-information experiment with the exact solver shows that planning with telemetry-derived rather than distance-based transit times lowers total cost by 2.95% on average, rising to 10.7% for high-value, fast-decaying produce, and that noisy or under-reported telemetry erodes this benefit. The ledger is treated as a conceptual data source whose latency and sensor trust remain to be tested.

HySec-ID: A Hybrid Representation and Ensemble Learning Framework for MQTT Intrusion Detection

Securing Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT)
communication is challenging because large numbers of constrained devices exchange traffic through a central broker. Attacks directed at this broker can interrupt communication among publishers and subscribers and affect multiple IoT services simultaneously. To address this problem,
this paper introduces HySec-ID, an intrusion-detection framework that combines conventional machine-learning classifiers with deep representation models. MQTT records are cleaned, encoded, and transformed into protocol, flow, temporal, and relational feature views. Random Forest and XGBoost analyse the structured attributes, while transformer- and
graph-based components capture dependencies that may not be evident from individual records. A fusion layer combines the confidence scores produced by these models to determine whether the observed traffic is benign or malicious. Experiments conducted on the considered MQTT intrusion dataset produced an accuracy of 98.72%, macro precision of 98.68%, macro recall of 98.71%, and macro F1-score of 98.69%. The receiver-operating-characteristic analysis yielded an AUC of 0.94. Within
the evaluated dataset, these findings show that combining multiple traffic representations provides balanced MQTT attack detection and reduces dependence on a single classifier.

An Evidence-Calibrated Framework for Detecting and Quantifying Cross-Split Leakage in Image Classification Benchmarks

Data leakage between training and evaluation partitions can produce overly optimistic estimates of generalization in visual benchmarks. Near-duplicate and transformed images may cross dataset splits through web crawling, video redundancy, and uncurated data ingestion, allowing deep neural networks to exploit memorization rather than semantic generalization. This paper presents an evidence-calibrated framework to detect, audit, and quantify cross-split leakage in image classification benchmarks. The pipeline extracts complementary embeddings using ResNet-50, Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16), and CLIP (ViT-B/32), then retrieves candidate pairs through FAISS approximate nearest-neighbor search. On CPU hardware, retrieval reduces query latency by up to 3.20× while maintaining 100% top-k candidate recall. Candidate pairs are assessed through multi-evidence score fusion, with feature weights and decision thresholds calibrated only on a held-out validation split to distinguish visual contamination from legitimate within-class similarity. A four-tier taxonomy classifies pairs as exact duplicates, transformed near-duplicates, semantic matches, or unrelated pairs. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST show that multi-backbone fusion improves leakage-detection F1-score from 41.7% for single-backbone heuristics to 87.0%, while regularized learned calibration achieves 100.0%. Downstream classification experiments further show that leakage can inflate evaluation accuracy by up to 4.0 percentage points. These results demonstrate the importance of rigorous cross-split auditing for trustworthy benchmark evaluation.

A Healthcare Workload Data Placement Framework Using  Hybrid Blockchain Storage Architecture

Modern healthcare systems today generate heterogeneous datasets with varying confidentiality, integrity, access, update, growth, and query requirements. Thus, the fixed allocation of on-chain and off-chain storage cannot balance security, scalability, and performance. Permissioned blockchain platforms such as Hyperledger Fabric provide integrity, auditability, identity-based access control, and Private Data Collections (PDCs); however, maintaining high-volume and frequently processed operational data on blockchain introduces considerable transaction, replication, and storage overhead. This paper presents a healthcare data placement framework for hybrid blockchain storage integrating the Fabric Ledger, PDCs, and heterogeneous off-chain databases. The proposed framework introduces a two-stage placement mechanism. First, security and workload constraints determine placement eligibility across the Ledger, PDC, and off-chain tiers based on restricted visibility, integrity and auditability requirements, update frequency, data growth, and query characteristics. PII is not treated as an exclusive placement criterion; both PII and non-PII data may reside on the Ledger when authorized shared visibility and blockchain-backed integrity are required. Second, for off-chain-eligible data, measured optimized latency and data-model requirements guide selection among MariaDB, CouchDB, and LevelDB. Identical healthcare workloads are evaluated using batch writes, indexed and non-indexed reads, complex analytical queries, ordering-service tuning, and storage-specific query optimization. The results reveal distinct storage-specific trade-offs that are transformed into reproducible placement rules. Off-chain integrity is retained through administrator-approved SHA-256 hash anchoring on Fabric, combining operational performance with blockchain-backed tamper verification.

CLSP-IoT: Cross-Layer Security and Performance Optimization for Resource-Constrained Wireless IoT Networks

Wireless Internet of Things networks support healthcare, smart cities, industrial automation, and transportation, but their open communication channels and constrained devices create a difficult balance between security and operational efficiency. Security mechanisms deployed independently at the physical, medium-access, network, and application layers often duplicate processing, increase signalling, consume energy, and delay packet delivery. This paper proposes CLSP-IoT, a cross-layer security and performance framework that integrates lightweight device authentication, machine-learning-based intrusion detection, and adaptive secure routing. The framework combines channel observations, traffic behaviour, routing state, node trust, residual energy, and communication reliability to coordinate protection across protocol layers. Lightweight authentication restricts network participation and establishes session keys. Cross-layer intrusion detection classifies normal and malicious behaviour using physical, traffic, and routing features. Adaptive routing then avoids suspicious or unreliable forwarding nodes while considering energy and delay. The framework is evaluated using ns-3 with synthetic normal and attack traffic. Throughput, packet delivery ratio, packet loss, latency, energy consumption, reliability, and intrusion-detection accuracy are examined. The reported results indicate that coordinated protection can improve attack detection and routing reliability while controlling communication and processing overhead. CLSP-IoT therefore provides a practical foundation for scalable security in resource-constrained wireless IoT deployments.
